response:
Both suites run, both fixes falsified against live code, replacements implemented and measured. Report:

---

# Verdicts

**Fix 1 (`_VERDICT_RE`): REFUTED as written.** The problem is real and your numbers are exact; the patch as drafted lets one model delete a finding by repetition.
**Fix 2 (arm 4b): REFUTED as written.** It fixes what you say it fixes, but it manufactures a phantom **CRITICAL** from a code fence and does weaken the exp43 guard.

Both are repairable without losing anything. I implemented and measured the repairs. Test suite: `4 failed, 4672 passed` — identical to HEAD (all 4 pre-existing; I verified by stashing).

---

## Fix 1

**Reproduced exactly.** 2,407 real replies: verdicts `6070 → 6804`, `+734`, 10.79%; Gemini 368, Codex 177, ChatGPT 154, DeepSeek 29, CC2 6. Zero regressions. Nothing to dispute in the measurement.

**Where I differ from the brief.** The driver is not `DESCRIPTION:`. Across all 734, only five labels ever occur: `VERDICT` 444 (60%), `FIND` 135, `DESCRIPTION` 134, `FINDING_ID` 19, `PROPOSED_FIX` 2. The dominant case is a model writing `VERDICT: CONFIRM C0007` — cleaner than the case you argued from.

**"Is it too permissive — what real text would it wrongly promote?"** Eight of twelve adversarial constructions are promoted: `FORMAT:`, `EXAMPLE:`, `TEMPLATE:`, `OUTPUT:`, `STATUS:`, `IF TRUE:`, `NOT A VERDICT:`, `> INSTRUCTION:`. Zero occur in today's archive, but these are precisely what a schema-echoing model emits, and your directives teach the schema.

**The disqualifying defect.** `add_verdict` does not dedupe; `auto_resolve_contested` counts verdict **rows**, not distinct models. The patch adds 28 duplicate `(type, cid)` rows (55 → 83). Running the live code:

```
NEW (patched): verdicts=4 status=REFUTED      ← one model, one reply
OLD (HEAD)  : verdicts=0 status=CONTESTED
  Auto-refuted C0001: 4 challenges, 0 defences in last 3 rounds
```

One model restating one CHALLENGE across four field labels auto-refutes a severity-0.9 finding. **That is a vote deleting a finding** — the thing this project exists to prevent. The underlying bug is pre-existing (three plain lines do it under HEAD, I checked), but Fix 1 opens it to replies that previously contributed nothing at all.

**"Verdict without its FIND/FOLLOW evidence — right outcome?"** Partly not: 169 of 369 recovered CONFIRMs carry empty evidence, and 101 MERGEs are recovered of which 2 have unresolvable sources — which `_resolve_merge_source` silently converts to CONFIRM, the inversion your own comment at line 2300 warns about.

**Replacement (implemented, tested).** Whitelist the five observed labels; dedupe `(type, cid)` per reply keeping the longest evidence.

```
verdicts: 6721   (HEAD 6070, permissive 6804 — the 83 discarded are duplicate rows)
all 8 adversarial labels: 0 matches;  VERDICT:/DESCRIPTION:/FIND: still 1 each
single-model veto falsifier: 4 rows → 1 verdict, status stays CONTESTED, evidence preserved
71 existing verdict tests pass
```

This **enhances** the schema: it recovers 651 genuine verdicts and closes a vote-based deletion path.

---

## Fix 2

**Verified where you claim it.** On the latest rehearsal (`sim45_memory_20260901T003907Z`): findings `10 → 31`, criticals `0 → 2`, agents contributing `2 → 6`. It does break the VACUOUS CURVE. `flaw_class=1` is defensible — in the current diff it is not hardcoded, it is `_parse_flaw_class`'s default, same as arm 4. (Your question describes `runner_core_prop.py`, the older draft, which *did* hardcode it.) No runaway recursion.

**Two of your numbers do not reproduce.**
- "round 0: 4 → 17" — I measure **3 → 12**. No sim45 `round_00` gives 4 → 17.
- "exactly 1 of 2,401 (0.04%)" — the shape occurs in **43 of 2,407 real replies (1.79%)**, 45× your figure. Your detector ran on raw text; `_parse_findings_core` strips `**` and code fences *before* arm 4b sees it, so bold-wrapped and fenced headings become plain headings.

**So "rehearsal fidelity, not real yield" is false.** Seven real replies change: real findings `4309 → 4330`, real criticals **`2620 → 2629`**. Nine new criticals across exp30, exp31, exp37, exp39, exp42 — it moves the critical series on five archived real runs. Six of the seven were previously the lossy `UNSTRUCTURED` fallback, so most of this is an improvement (exp37 r15 is genuine four-finding panel work HEAD dropped to zero). But it is not "almost nothing for real runs."

**"Does it weaken the guards?" Yes — demonstrated.** A `## Review: Round 8 Summary` citing C0019/C0020 with `### F001` headings registers 2 findings at 0.5. The fallback suppresses exactly this (exp43 C0040); arm 4b runs before it and is not subject to it. You are right that the specific archived reply has zero markdown F-headers — I confirmed both review-summary replies in the archive have 0 — but that is an instance check, and the guard is a class guard.

**The phantom critical — the finding that matters most.** Fence-stripping at lines 437–438 runs *before* arm 4b, so a heading inside a ``` fence is promoted to a real heading:

```
model says "I found nothing", quotes the schema in a fence
  HEAD → 1 finding, Gemini_UNSTRUCTURED, sev 0.3
  NEW  → 1 finding, Gemini_F001, sev 0.9  ← CRITICAL, desc '<short title of the defect>'
```

This is your "manufacture a critical" case, arriving not through the 0.5 default but through fence-stripping. Against a gate that keys on novel CRITICALs, a reply reporting *nothing* can now block or distort convergence.

**Severity 0.5 is safe**, separately: `CRITICAL_SEVERITY_THRESHOLD = 0.7`, so the default cannot mint a critical, and word severities survive (`SEVERITY: critical` → 0.9 via `_normalise_field_labels`). But it is inconsistent with the pre-existing `### Finding N:` adapter at line 445, which defaults the same class of input to **0.7** — deliberately critical. Two markdown-heading adapters, opposite defaults.

**Also admitted: a model's own retraction.** exp37 r15 F050 reads `FIND: Actually, no bug found... ANALYSE: REJECTED. My initial suspicion was incorrect` — registered as a finding at 0.5.

**Replacement (implemented, tested).** Accept only headings that exist outside fences in the pre-strip text; apply the fallback's review-summary guard to arm 4b.

```
fenced schema example        -> 0.3 fallback (was 0.9 CRITICAL)
review summary w/ F-headings -> 0 findings (was 2)
genuine md finding           -> 0.8, preserved
REAL yield: 4330 findings / 2629 criticals — IDENTICAL to your version
SIM: 97 → 90 findings, same 9 criticals — 7 rehearsal false positives removed
suite: same 4 pre-existing failures, no new ones
```

Full real-archive recall at zero cost, with the critical-manufacturing vector closed.

---

## Anomalies you did not name

**1. The test suite shreds the archive.** `python3 -m pytest bench/tests/ -q` — the command in your brief — rewrites two tracked verbatim panel records, deleting **2,282 lines** and replacing verbatim model responses with `## Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview (ge) — NO RESPONSE FILE`. Isolated: `TestUsageTextAdvertisesOnlyImplementedFlags` → 2 files modified; `TestEveryScriptCompiles` → 0. It executes `scripts/assemble_panel_record.py` / `_0819.py` as subprocesses to probe `--help`; those have no `if __name__ == "__main__"` guard, so the module body runs and calls `dest.write_text(...)` against a log dir that is not there. It cost me a `git stash pop` mid-review. For a project whose deliverable is archived verbatim panel records, this outranks both parser bugs.

**2. `_parse_flaw_class` is non-deterministic.** Line 316: `return (abs(hash(key)) % 8) + 1`. `hash()` on `str` is salted per process. The docstring claims "deterministic hash ... to ensure consistent mapping without corrupting metrics" — it does the opposite. Measured: 4 archived replies get a different flaw_class every run (same finding → class 2, 4, 5 under seeds 0/1/2). Any flaw-class distribution in any experiment is irreproducible. One-line fix: `hashlib.sha1`. This contaminated my own A/B until I pinned `PYTHONHASHSEED` — worth knowing before you measure anything class-keyed.

**3. Code-leak guard has a hole.** `_CODE_LEAK_VARNAMES` omits `str`; the archive parses to a live finding id `Gemini_str`.

**4. 972 of 2,485 archived replies (39%) are stored truncated at exactly 10,000 characters**, ending mid-token (`bench/insect_brain.py:980`, `label: text[:10000]`, still live). Every archive measurement here — your 2,414 and 2,401 denominators, and all of mine — is computed over truncated text. It biases *against* both fixes (findings and verdicts past 10k are invisible), so the recovery figures are floors.

**5.** `_proposed.patch` does not exist in the working copy; I read the changes from `git diff`.

---

## Bottom line

Neither fix detracts from the schema in intent — both target real, measured loss of panel work, and your instinct that the panel's output was not reaching the pipeline is correct and now demonstrated. Both detract in their current form: Fix 1 by letting one model's repetition refute a finding, Fix 2 by minting a critical from quoted schema. With the two repairs above, adopt both. Adopt Fix 1's repair first — it is the one that currently converts model agreement into a deletion.
